items.title: the spirit object: the node api for face apps
items.box:
GOAL/G32: THE SPIRIT OBJECT, THE NODE API FOR FACE APPS (from goal/G30.22)

A face app needs a spirit object that packages every call on the home node into something easy to use, so no app hand-rolls a call again.

THE SPIRIT OBJECT
- One file, hand-coded and rock solid, using helper modules from the home node where needed; the relay serves it as the very first script, inline in the one html file it serves (face.html).
- It is assembled from the api.js every family folder holds, the node's and the servers', one member per family: spirit.fs., spirit.jobs., spirit.chatClerver. and so on, each verb asynchronous; the fs family keeps the kernel's names (loadFile, loadDataUrl, statFile, getAnnotations, saveFile, deleteFile); error(), formatBytes() and escapeHtml() are the object's own.
- It runs in a page at home, on the face, and in a server process (goal/G32.3).
- The apps use it, and nothing else, to reach the node.

ITS CHECKS
- The page's check is complete: every argument of every call is checked before the call goes out, its shape and its field rules (peer keys, labels, descriptions and every other field), so a malformed call never leaves the page.
- The field rules are js/fieldRules.js, the one definition both sides use; the node stays the gate and still checks everything it checks.
- An input field refuses what its rule would refuse as it is typed (it takes no more characters past the limit), never telling how far past the limit the text went.

THE RETROFIT
- This goal builds the object (goal/G32.1), moves the face code onto it (goal/G32.2) and the servers (goal/G32.3); when it is done, no hand-made call to the node or a server is left anywhere.
- Each home-only app moves onto it when it moves to the face, in its own item (chatter in goal/G7).
- The kernel's synchronous browser helpers stay for the old shell until its last user is gone.

items.title: the spirit object: node api, async, checked
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
THE SPIRIT OBJECT

- One file, hand-coded and rock solid, using helper modules from the home node where needed.
- The relay serves it as the very first script, inline in face.html; the home node's index.html loads it too, so an app finds the same object at home and on the face; it runs in node too, for server processes, on the node's loopback door.
- Every family folder holds its api.js: the node's families (js/fs/, js/jobs/, js/contact/ ...) as the servers' (goal/G32.3); each is written by its family's author to the node's standard (one shape, the same checks), and the node delivers it to the caller, as introSpector reads the family folders; a server never hears of it.
- This item writes the node's families' api.js (js/fs/, js/jobs/, js/contact/ and the rest).
- The spirit object is assembled from them, one member per family: spirit.fs., spirit.jobs., spirit.contact., spirit.chatClerver. and so on, each verb an asynchronous function.
- The fs family keeps the kernel's names beside its verbs: spirit.fs.loadFile(), loadDataUrl(), statFile(), getAnnotations(), saveFile(), deleteFile(); and the helpers error(), formatBytes(), escapeHtml() are the object's own.
- Each family's api.js carries the checks for its own fields, most of them by the one shared js/fieldRules.js; no verb declaration changes.
- The one file served first and inline holds the core: the transport, the checks, the helpers, and the assembling.
- Its calls go through the transport the page has: the sealed link on the face, the node's own door at home.
- Its check is complete: every argument of every call is checked before it goes out, its shape and its field rules (peer keys, labels, descriptions and every other field), with js/fieldRules.js, the one definition both sides use; a malformed call never leaves the page; the node stays the gate.
- Its red calls it, in a page and in node, with good and malformed arguments and sees the malformed ones refused in the page.
- It ends with a relay tag.

Where: face.html, the file, index.html. Blocks goal/G32.2, goal/G32.3.

items.title: the face code moves onto the spirit object
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
THE FACE CODE MOVES ONTO THE SPIRIT OBJECT

- The shell elements, Files, Contacts, Join, Media Viewer, Apps and Icons reach the node only through the spirit object; no hand-made verb call is left in them.
- Their input fields refuse what their rule would refuse as it is typed (no characters past the limit), never telling how far past the limit the text went.
- Each home-only app moves onto the object when it moves to the face, in its own item (chatter in goal/G7); the kernel's synchronous browser helpers stay for the old shell until its last user is gone.
- Its red: no hand-made verb call left in that code, and an input stops at its limit.

Where: shell/js/, shell/files, shell/contacts, shell/join, shell/mediaViewer, shell/apps, shell/icons. Blocked by goal/G32.1.

items.title: server retrofit onto the spirit object
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
THE SERVERS MOVE ONTO THE SPIRIT OBJECT

- Every server process under process/js reaches the node only through the spirit object (goal/G32.1), running in node on the node's loopback door; no hand-made call (askNode, kernel.core.ask with the node's url) is left.
- The same functions and the same complete check as a page has.
- Every server with verbs ships a small api.js in its family folder (process/js/<name>/<name>.family/api.js, beside its verbs' descriptions; a server without that folder gets one), written by the server's author to the node's standard and delivered by the node to the caller without the server hearing of it, as introSpector reads the family folders: its verbs as async functions with the checks for their arguments, riding the spirit object's transport; it is the spirit object's member of that name, so chatter calls spirit.chatClerver.lineWrite({to, text, re}).
- Its red: no hand-made node call left in process/js, and every server with verbs ships its api.js.
- When the goal is done, all of it is cleaned up: no hand-made call to the node or to a server left anywhere.

Where: process/js/*. Blocked by goal/G32.1.
